speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: A strong defence safeguards Singapore’s sovereignty and ensures peace and security for Singaporeans’ pursuit of economic and social progress.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The geopolitical and security landscape Singapore faces is becoming more volatile and complex.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and rising contestation between the United States and China have reduced trust among countries.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Divisions are rising in different spheres, while the multilateral rules-based order that has underpinned cross-border cooperation and conflict resolution is unravelling.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Access to a growing range of sophisticated technologies has enabled malicious actors to pose significant security threats, including terrorist acts, hostile information campaigns, and cyberattacks on critical infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Amidst these turbulent times, steady and long-term investment in a strong defence is critical.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) and SAF are transforming to deter and defend against emerging and evolving threats in multiple domains, across the spectrum from peace to war.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Technology remains a key force multiplier for the SAF.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We will employ more unmanned platforms to extend the reach and survivability of our forces.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: For more timely and accurate operational decision-making, the SAF will build up its digital capabilities and deploy data analytics and artificial intelligence in future command and control information systems.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The DIS will develop a digital range to train our forces under realistic cyberattack scenarios and set up a Digital Ops-Tech Centre to enable our operational and defence technology workforces to collaborate on new digital solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Beyond utilising military technologies, we will expand our use of “dual-use” technologies and collaborate with a wider range of technology partners.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We are also enhancing our training infrastructure to maintain the SAF’s edge.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: By the end of this year, the SAF’s new Instrumented Battle Circuits will provide more realistic training under simulated artillery bombardment and air strikes, allowing our soldiers to hone operational instincts and tactical fundamentals.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Our investments in overseas facilities such as the Shoalwater Bay Training Area in Australia will allow the SAF to conduct large-scale exercises that cannot be replicated locally.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Even as it enhances training effectiveness, the SAF will not compromise on the safety of our servicemen.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The SAF’s adoption of an enterprise Safety Information System will enable important safety reminders and lessons to reach its service personnel quickly.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Through the newly launched Heat Resilience and Performance Centre, we will conduct research to better prevent heat injury and boost our soldiers’ resilience against heat stress amid rising global temperatures.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We will continue to strengthen the NS system.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We will maximise the contributions of our national servicemen by reviewing our medical classification system, expanding work-learn schemes for our Full-Time National Servicemen, and redesigning vocational roles.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Operationally Ready National Servicemen will also see expanded opportunities to apply their civilian expertise in operational contexts.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We will also improve the NS experience, by reviewing policies and procedures and deploying technology to make NS processes and services more efficient and convenient, so that national servicemen can focus on training to remain operationally ready.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We will also continue to enhance support and recognition for our national servicemen.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: As a small nation state, we must uphold a global order and regional security architecture that is based on openness, inclusivity, and adherence to international law and norms.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Bilaterally, we will continue to strengthen defence relations with our neighbours, Malaysia and Indonesia.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We will also expand cooperation with partners such as Australia, China, India, and the United States, through high-level dialogue, military-to-military exchanges, and joint training.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Every Singaporean has a part to play in keeping our home peaceful, safe, and secure.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We will pursue new ways to encourage Singaporeans to participate actively in Total Defence.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Building on the 2023 Total Defence Community Exercise, we will partner more communities to enhance individual and collective emergency preparedness and resilience in the face of potential crises.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We will encourage more ground-up initiatives from Singaporeans to put Total Defence into action.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Our defence and military museums are being revamped, and a new NS Gallery will open by 2027 to bring our defence story to life for Singaporeans.
